correctness.rationale: Bunnett--Namanya's full text identifies the automorphism group of the smooth syzygy hypersurface with the projective stabilizer of its four-dimensional coefficient space. For the displayed special member, the annihilator pencil is \(U=\langle z_0z_2,z_1z_2\rangle\), with reduced base scheme \(V(z_2)\cup\{[0:0:1]\}\). A stabilizer must preserve the line and isolated point separately; conversely every projective transformation preserving that pair preserves \(U\). Thus the stabilizer is represented by \(\operatorname{diag}(A,c)\), and quotienting common scalars gives \(\operatorname{GL}_2\). The included symbolic replay independently gives stabilizer Lie-algebra dimension \(4\) in \(\mathfrak{pgl}_3\), consistent with the global proof.

originality.rationale: The primary preprint exhibits only a faithful diagonal-torus action on its explicit special member and does not state its full automorphism group. Exact-equation, annihilator-pencil, syzygy-bundle, projective-stabilizer, and \(\operatorname{GL}_2\) searches found no checked source implying the complete group calculation. The same source's general-member argument concerns a four-point base locus, whereas the present base locus is a line plus an isolated point, so the two stabilizer statements are not implication-equivalent.
residual_risks: A later revision, unindexed note, or literature source using a different presentation of the same projective bundle may independently contain the exact \(\operatorname{GL}_2\) calculation; none was found in the checked sources.

value.rationale: The source highlights this explicit smooth member precisely to demonstrate a jump from generic finiteness to positive-dimensional automorphisms. Replacing the exhibited torus lower bound by the complete connected group \(\operatorname{GL}_2\), and hence the exact tangent dimension \(4\), gives structural information about the exceptional stratum and identifies non-diagonal symmetries invisible in the source's example. This is a natural exact invariant of a source-selected exceptional object rather than an arbitrary finite computation.
